_comment: MCP tool definitions for the iterative planner. Single source of truth for tool schemas, descriptions, and phase mappings. Read by mcp_server.mjs at startup.

create_plan.description: Create a new iterative plan with a goal. This is the first step — describe what you want to accomplish.

goal.description: What you want to accomplish (1-2 sentences)

resume_plan.description: Resume the currently active plan. Returns current state, phase, and what to do next.

list_plans.description: List all plans (active and archived) with their status.

read_kb.description: Read the knowledge base (mistakes, patterns, gotchas). MUST be called before adding findings. Returns KB content and generates a digest hash.

add_finding.description: Add an indexed finding from your exploration. Minimum 3 findings required before transitioning to PLAN. Each finding must have a title, context, and impact (at least 30 words).

context.description: Detailed context — what you found and why it matters (minimum 30 words)

check_adjacency.description: Run blast radius analysis on files you plan to modify. Identifies related files that may also need changes.

files.description: Files to analyze for adjacency impacts

set_problem_statement.description: Define the problem statement for your plan. Must include: (1) expected behavior, (2) current behavior, (3) root cause.

list_files_to_modify.description: Declare every file that will be touched during EXECUTE. This scopes the work and enables drift detection.

files.description: Files to modify with action and justification

add_step.description: Add an execution step to the plan. Steps should be atomic and ordered.

define_verification.description: Define verification strategy with success criteria. Each criterion needs a test command and expected result.

request_approval.description: Request user approval to proceed from PLAN to EXECUTE. Blocked until problem statement, file list, and verification strategy are defined.

summary.description: Brief summary of the plan for user review

update_progress.description: Mark a step as completed or update its status. Updates progress.md and state.md.

notes.description: What was done or why it's blocked

log_change.description: Log a file change to the change manifest in state.md.

create_checkpoint.description: Create a checkpoint before a risky operation. Enables rollback if something goes wrong.

add_red_team_vector.description: Add a red-team attack vector. Minimum 3 vectors required before transitioning to REFLECT. Each needs: attack description, impact, and mitigation.

attack.description: How could this change be exploited or fail?

mitigation.description: How is this prevented or contained?

add_verification_result.description: Record a verification result (PASS/FAIL) with evidence. Must include actual command output as proof of work.

update_kb.description: Update the knowledge base with lessons learned. Add mistakes (M-NNN), patterns (P-NNN), or gotchas (G-NNN).

id.description: Entry ID (e.g., M-006, P-008). Required unless type is 'none'.

content.description: Full content of the KB entry

reason_if_none.description: Why no new learnings (required if type is 'none')

write_summary.description: Write the plan summary for CLOSE phase. Summarizes what was done, what changed, and key decisions.

get_state.description: Get the current plan state including phase, iteration, step, and transition history.

get_gate_status.description: Check the status of all gates — which have passed, which are blocking, and what's needed to proceed.

get_plan_info.description: Get the current plan details including goal, findings, steps, and progress.

request_human_help.description: Escalate to the human user when stuck. Use when all available tools are blocked or you need guidance.

diagnose_gate.description: Diagnose why a gate is blocked. Returns the Prolog guards that are failing, what each guard requires, which MCP tool to call to satisfy it, and any invariant violations. Use this when get_gate_status shows a FAIL.

gate.description: Gate name to diagnose (e.g., 'explore-to-plan', 'plan-to-execute', 'reflect-to-validate', 'validate-to-close'). If omitted, diagnoses the next gate for the current phase.
